clue.text: Appeal by artist to orchestra for some dance music

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
a band is a group of musicians playing together

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a painter to get the orchestra to play a dance tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Spanish triple-time dance, and the slow movement written for it in Baroque suites.

clue.text: Lover boy called for a drink

indicators.note: called means spoken out, so the word for the lover boy is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: an amoretto is a little Cupid, the boy god of love in Italian painting

explanation.surface: A young romantic shouts an order at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' signals a sound-alike: AMORETTO, the Italian painter's cherub of love, said aloud gives the almond liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, served as an after-dinner tipple.

clue.text: A young man's given warning about diamonds in treasure store

indicators.note: about means going around, so the young man's letters wrap round what follows

parts.note: a lad is a young man, with the possessive S kept
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
taken as written
cave is Latin for 'beware', British schoolboy slang for a warning that a teacher is coming

explanation.surface: A youth, cautioned over some gems, is caught near a hoard of valuables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but wraps the young man round the gems. 'given warning' is CAVE, Latin 'beware', the lookout's cry at British public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Arabian Nights tale, a cavern full of riches, now any place crammed with valuables.

clue.text: A game fighter, perhaps, needs a careful defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
a GI is an American soldier, one kind of fighter

explanation.surface: A plucky combatant requires a well-considered justification.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written justification of one's opinions or conduct, as in Newman's famous work.

clue.text: Killer? Resolve to arrest one

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the resolving word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to resolve is to decide
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A detective resolves to bring in the murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this killer is a particular kind: one who kills a god.
explanation.definitionFit: A god-killer: the killing of a deity, or the person who does it.

clue.text: Type of tank cleaned initially after the first of the month

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: the first day of September can be written Sept I, with I the Roman one

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of cleaned

explanation.surface: A tank gets a clean at the start of each month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first of the month' reads as Sept. I, a date; 'initially' takes C from cleaned and 'after' puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewage tank in which waste is broken down by bacteria, used where there is no mains drain.

clue.text: Understands sarcastic remarks

explanation.surface: Someone gets the joke behind the barbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'dig' means grasp or appreciate; a dig is also a cutting jibe aimed at someone.

clue.text: Listener puzzle in part of Ireland

indicators.note: puzzle as a verb means confuse, so the letters of the previous word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Listener crossword set in an Irish province.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard British crossword in The Times; here its name is the fodder and 'puzzle' scrambles it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four historic provinces of Ireland, in the east, around Dublin.

clue.text: Monarch's duty-bound to keep physically fit

indicators.note: bound means tied up or enclosed, so the tax word wraps round the royal letters

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: The King or Queen is obliged to stay in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty-bound' reads as one word meaning obliged, but it splits: the tax is the duty and 'bound' tells it to enclose the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To train the body through regular physical activity.

clue.text: Soldier repulsed in war, apparently

indicators.note: repulsed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fighting man is driven back in battle, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters inside 'war, apparently' (ARAP) and 'repulsed' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for paratrooper, a soldier trained to drop by parachute.

clue.text: From shop, garments dispatched shortly

parts.note: delicates are fine garments needing gentle washing

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to be dispatched is to be sent

explanation.surface: Clothes are sent off from a store without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but trims SENT to SEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: One on the move after retiring

definitions.text: One on the move after retiring

parts.words: One on the move after retiring
parts.note: retiring here means going to bed, so this is someone who walks about while asleep, not a pensioner

explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker gets up and wanders after going to bed.

clue.text: Group of players failing to finish series

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is lost

parts.note: the ... are the ... section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A team falls short of completing a run of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchestral section loses its final S; 'Group of players' tempts as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A succession of linked things, as in a run of wins or a chain of events.

clue.text: Evidence perhaps supplied by university teacher without a word of hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the teacher's letters surround the pause

parts.note: a docent is a university lecturer, chiefly in the US
um is the sound people make while hesitating

explanation.surface: A lecturer produces proof without ever pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but takes its old sense of 'outside': the American-style lecturer surrounds the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper or record, which can be produced as proof in court, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Poet a doctor found lacking in energy

indicators.note: lacking in means one letter is missing from the doctor

parts.note: a houseman is a junior hospital doctor in Britain
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A medic is found to be a writer of verse, though rather lethargic.
explanation.walkthrough: A.E. Housman wrote A Shropshire Lad; HOUSEMAN, a British junior hospital doctor, loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A.E. Housman, English poet and classical scholar, author of A Shropshire Lad.

clue.text: Governor in favour of invading former communist town

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title given to a colonial governor

indicators.note: invading means entering, so one piece goes into the middle of another

parts.note: red was the label for a communist in Cold War days
for means in favour of

explanation.surface: A ruler supports an attack on a town once run by Communists.
explanation.walkthrough: A British colonial governor is styled His Excellency; 'former communist' tempts towards an ex-Soviet town, but it is just the old label red.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in the west of England, county town of Herefordshire.

clue.text: China fronts state conference

indicators.note: fronts means stands in front of, so this piece leads the next

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
to aver is to state

explanation.surface: Porcelain leads the agenda at a national summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country or porcelain: Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, often tedious discussion or parley, from Portuguese palavra.

clue.text: Officer has to adapt, having dismissed second soldier

indicators.note: having dismissed means a letter is sent away from the word before

parts.note: to adapt is to adjust
a soldier ant is one of the defending caste in an ant colony

explanation.surface: An officer must change, having sacked his second soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' is the insect, not a military man.
explanation.definitionFit: A military staff officer who assists the commanding officer with administration.

clue.text: Engineers put in notice — faulty building

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the engineers go into the notice
faulty means defective, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers post a notice about a defective structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' puts RE into NOTICE and 'faulty' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that has been put up, or the act of constructing it.

clue.text: Customer in the Saracen's head, on the wagon

indicators.note: on means placed above, as in a down clue
head means the opening letter of Saracen's

parts.note: a hopper is a railway wagon that tips its load out through the floor

explanation.surface: A drinker at the Saracen's Head pub has signed the pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Saracen's Head is a common British pub name; 'on the wagon' (teetotal) hides the hopper wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to the stores to buy things.

clue.text: Monarch's distorted language

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Monarch's including the S

explanation.surface: A sovereign's speech is garbled.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of the possessive is fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romance tongue spoken in the Swiss canton of Graubünden.

clue.text: In day off work, avoided lake, for one, in cutter

indicators.note: avoided says one letter is left out, with another taking its place

parts.note: a sickle is a curved blade for cutting crops
I is the Roman one

explanation.surface: On leave, someone skipped the lake trip to go sailing in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a boat, but it is the tool; 'avoided lake, for one' removes L and puts I in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British for a day taken off claiming to be ill.

clue.text: Patient man with teaching qualification worked occasionally

parts.note: Job in the Bible endured his trials with legendary patience
BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A tolerant teacher works part-time.
explanation.definitionFit: Did odd bits of casual paid work now and then.

clue.text: City first secured equipment for business

indicators.note: first says the following word comes before the city

parts.note: fixed means secured or fastened
a capital is a chief city

explanation.surface: A city's financial district first got its kit together.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term assets such as buildings and machinery that a firm keeps and uses.

clue.text: Photograph showing unknown boy

parts.note: x is the algebraic unknown
Ray is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A snapshot of an anonymous lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph, an image of inside the body.

clue.text: Flag regularly displayed in air raids

indicators.note: regularly displayed means every other letter is shown

explanation.surface: A banner is flown periodically during bombing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner but the yellow flag, a wild plant of the iris family.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild waterside plant, and flag is a general name for that flower.

clue.text: Strongly worded attack not starting here, by the way

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a broadside is a fierce verbal attack, like a ship's cannon volley

explanation.surface: A tirade that never quite begins, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like 'incidentally' but means beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: At the side of a road, as a café or verge stands by the way.

clue.text: Making assessment about collection of books in circulation

indicators.note: about means around, so the assessment surrounds the books

parts.note: rating is making an assessment
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A librarian evaluates books as they are passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection of books' is the Old Testament, not a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning round, going in a rota, as in a role taken in turns.
